## Speech Pathologist Salary Melbourne: Award Minimums and How to Convert

If you are researching the **speech pathologist salary Melbourne** market, the starting point is the minimum pay rates set by the Health Professionals and Support Services Award 2020 (MA000027). This award covers speech pathologists employed in private practice, hospitals, and community health. The rates below are from the Fair Work Ombudsman and apply from 1 October 2026.

### Minimum Hourly Rates Under the Award

For a Health Professional employee at Level 1, the minimum hourly rate depends on your qualification and experience. The award uses the Australian Qualifications Framework (AQF) Level 5 as the base for a speech pathologist (typically a bachelor’s degree).

| Experience | Hourly rate | Weekly rate (38 hours) |
|------------|-------------|------------------------|
| 1st year | $32.44 | $1,232.70 |
| 2nd–3rd year | $34.44 | $1,308.80 |
| 4th–6th year | $37.53 | $1,426.00 |
| 7th year+ | $40.56 | $1,541.30 |

These rates are the minimum. Many employers pay above award, but the award sets the legal floor. For comparison, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, so a speech pathologist’s minimum is well above that.

### Converting Hourly to Annual and Fortnightly Pay

To estimate your annual gross pay, use the formula:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

We assume a standard full-time week of 38 hours under the award. For a 1st-year speech pathologist:

- $32.44 × 38 = $1,232.72 per week
- $1,232.72 × 52 = $64,101.44 per year

Your fortnightly pay would be $1,232.72 × 2 = $2,465.44 before tax and super. This is a simple estimate; it does not include overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

### Casual Loading: 25% on Top

If you work as a casual speech pathologist, you are entitled to a 25% loading on the base hourly rate. This compensates for not receiving paid leave or other entitlements. The casual loading is paid for all ordinary hours and is in addition to any penalty rates.

For a 1st-year casual:

- Base rate: $32.44
- Casual loading: 25% of $32.44 = $8.11
- Casual rate: $40.55 per hour

When using [the timesheet](/), never enter a rate that already includes casual loading. Instead, enter the base hourly rate and tick the casual loading checkbox. The tool will add the 25% automatically.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Employers must pay superannuation guarantee contributions of 12% on your ordinary earnings. This is paid on top of your gross pay, not deducted from it. For a full-time speech pathologist earning $64,101 per year, the employer contributes an extra $7,692.17 into your super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830.

Super is calculated on your base rate plus any loadings or penalties that are part of ordinary earnings. It does not apply to overtime or expense reimbursements. For more details, see our guide on [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your annual gross pay is subject to income tax and the Medicare levy. For 2026–27, the resident tax rates are:

- $0–$18,200: nil
- $18,201–$45,000: 15% on excess over $18,200
- $45,001–$135,000: 30% on excess over $45,000
- $135,001–$190,000: 37% on excess over $135,000
- Above $190,000: 45%

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income, with reductions for lower incomes. The tax-free threshold is included. For a speech pathologist earning $64,101, the estimated tax would be around $10,000–$11,000 plus Medicare of about $1,280. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a more precise estimate.

### Fortnightly Pay in Context

Many employers pay fortnightly. For a 1st-year speech pathologist, the fortnightly gross is $2,465.44. After tax and Medicare, you might take home around $1,900–$2,000. Casual employees receive the loading, so their fortnightly gross would be higher, but they also need to budget for unpaid leave.

### Where to Find More Information

- [Pay guides](/blog) – Download the official Health Professionals Award pay guide from the Fair Work Ombudsman.
- [Casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) – Understand how loading interacts with penalty rates.
- [Average pay](/topics/average-pay) – Compare award rates to Australian Bureau of Statistics data for health professionals.

Remember, the figures here are minimums. Your actual speech pathologist salary in Melbourne may be higher depending on experience, location, and employer. Always check your employment contract and the award for your specific classification.
